judged_text: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are absent, so the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op that silently discards every team member's destination calendar. Collective bookings whose organizer has no destination calendar (the default for users who never chose one) accumulate team members' calendars into teamDestinationCalendars (~lines 987-992) and then drop them on the floor — the event is created only via the organizer's own credentials and members' destination calendars never receive it, defeating the PR's stated purpose for the most common organizer configuration.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exist (the final `: null` in the ternary around lines ~1040-1066). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional chaining makes this a silent no-op, so any `teamDestinationCalendars` gathered from other users (built in the `teamMemberPromises` loop around ~970-992) are discarded. This loss of data/behavior is directly introduced by the diff and is verifiable from the code shown.
